name: goodwill
quote: I'll give him the benefit of the doubt.
description: A willingness to show a person or group trust and kindness when you don't have a good reason to be nice to them.
perceptions: That person or group could use some support.
People react well to being trusted.

guidance.description: 18 methods for cultivating goodwill and abandoning ill will

examples: helping a stranger carry their groceries
giving money to a poor person

comparisons.description: 'Goodwill' can be part of reaction driven by a sense of 'compassion' for someone's suffering. But 'goodwill' can also be shown to people who are not suffering.

variations.name: goodwill mindset
variations.description: A pattern of belief that people react well to assuming their intentions are unselfish.
perceptions: That person or group could use some support.
People react well to being trusted.

variations.name: account of goodwill
variations.description: We may keep an internal tally of how much a person or group has earned or spent our positivity towards them.
perceptions: My desire to show trust and kindness to someone is not unlimited.
At some point, they should be appreciative and/or more self-sufficient.

comparisons.description: Having goodwill towards people doesn't have to blindly assume the optimistic best case. You might be aware that they might not 'do the right thing', but that treating them positively has a chance of encouraging pro-social behavior.
Goodwill doesn't necessarily involve being generous with time or materials - it can just be trust, kindness, and encouraging words.
Trusting a stranger with something important may involve faith in human nature.

We unconciously balance a 'trust account' for every person and social group. At a certain level of trust, we'll look at people differently, but each of us has a different level of trust required. 'Cynicism' is when the bar of trust is so high that you assume only a few people are trustworthy. 'Goodwill' is when the bar of trust is so low it includes most strangers. If the bar of trust is at the 'extended friends and family' level, you're normal.

commentaries.quote: You should be wary when your goodwill account with someone is getting low. If you get to a trust level of zero, the best case is that your benefactor walks away. There are many worse cases, some of them quite unpleasant. This goes whether you're a person, a company, a government, or a species.
Goodwill is the one and only asset that competition cannot undersell or destroy.
